lede: Public-domain maps, documents and photographs, each with its source.
credit: Pages and maps of congressional documents from the U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scans of govinfo.gov, and from the Internet Archive; newspaper pages from the Florida Digital Newspaper Library and congressional printings from the University of Florida Digital Collections; photographs and drawings of the Ocklawaha from the Library of Congress, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the State Archives of Florida via Wikimedia Commons. All in the public domain or CC0.

plates.caption: The report of the Senate's Select Committee on Roads and Canals on the bill for a survey of a canal route between the Atlantic and the Gulf: the work “not only practicable, but much more easily accomplished than former estimates and opinions have supposed.”
plates.source: Senate Document 21, 19th Congress, 1st Session, p. 1. U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.

plates.caption: The summary of Bernard and Poussin's report of 19 February 1829, from the foot of p. 65 to the head of p. 66, set together: the ridge of the peninsula 150 feet high on average, a ship channel “not practicable.”
plates.source: House Document 8, 23rd Congress, 2nd Session, pp. 65–66. U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.

plates.caption: The engineers' line from Tampa Bay past the “old Indian town O-ke-hum-ky” to the Ocklawaha: the ridge only 87 feet high there, but “the want of water precludes the practicability” of a canal.
plates.source: House Document 185, 22nd Congress, 1st Session, p. 44. U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.

plates.caption: Lieutenant Pickell's count of the water in the ponds near the summit: an excess of 45,883,438 cubic yards over what a canal for boats would need.
plates.source: House Document 185, 22nd Congress, 1st Session, p. 6. U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.

plates.caption: The instruction of November 1853 allowing the officer of the canal survey to examine a railroad as well, and the opening of his report on a line from Fernandina to Cedar Key.
plates.source: Senate Executive Document 76, 33rd Congress, 2nd Session, p. 2. U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.

plates.titel: A ship canal from the St. Marys, 1879
plates.caption: Map of the country embraced in the preliminary survey for a ship canal from the St. Marys River to the Gulf of Mexico, made in 1879 under Brevet Major General Q. A. Gillmore, with the profile of the canal across the ridge below.
plates.source: Senate Executive Document 154, 46th Congress, 2nd Session (1880), folding map. U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.

plates.caption: “Twenty-six million dollars has been subscribed to the capital stock of the Florida Ship Canal, and work will commence at once.”
plates.source: Ocala Banner-Lacon, 26 May 1883, p. 2. Florida Digital Newspaper Library, University of Florida; public domain.

plates.caption: The directors of the Florida Ship Canal and Transit Company adopt their chief engineer's report: a tidewater ship canal for $46,000,000.
plates.source: Ocala Banner, 1 September 1883, p. 3, detail. Florida Digital Newspaper Library, University of Florida; public domain.

plates.caption: “… has gone up in a soap bubble and bursted. The employes of the company are entering suit against the directors for unpaid salaries.”
plates.source: The Pensacolian, 23 August 1884, p. 1. Florida Digital Newspaper Library, University of Florida; public domain.

plates.caption: A board of Army engineers at Savannah proposes to survey five routes across northern Florida, a thousand miles in all.
plates.source: Ocala Evening Star, 21 May 1909, p. 1. Florida Digital Newspaper Library, University of Florida; public domain.

plates.titel: The Osceola in the Great Cypress Pass, 1886
plates.caption: The steamer Osceola in the Great Cypress Pass of the Ocklawaha. Photograph by George Barker of Niagara Falls.
plates.source: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs, cph.3b42152, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.

plates.caption: Page 20 of Lanier's Florida: the lumberman's complaint about the rain, the turn into the Ocklawaha, and Dick the pole-man asleep on the guards.
plates.source: Sidney Lanier, Florida (1875/76), p. 20; Internet Archive; public domain.

plates.caption: The stern-wheeler Marion on the Ocklawaha, drawn by J. Wells Champney for Edward King's series on the South; Lanier travelled on a boat of that name in 1875.
plates.source: Edward King, The Great South (1875), engraving after J. Wells Champney, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.

plates.titel: A cypress-shingle yard on the Ocklawaha, 1870
plates.caption: Harry Fenn's watercolour of a yard where shingles were split from cypress on the river: the timber work that the steamers carried and the logging that later choked the upper river.
plates.source: Harry Fenn, The Cypress-Shingle Yard, Ocklawaha River, Florida, watercolour, 1870; The Metropolitan Museum of Art 201672, via Wikimedia Commons; CC0.

plates.caption: Title page of the privately printed prospectus of the Atlantic & Gulf Ship Canal across the Peninsula of Florida, London 1877: “Only 20 Copies.”
plates.source: The Atlantic & Gulf Ship Canal across the Peninsula of Florida (London 1877), title page; Cornell University Library via Internet Archive; public domain.

plates.caption: Schedule card of Hart's Daily Line, Ocklawaha Navigation Company, Palatka, 14 February 1890, signed by H. L. Hart, general manager: the steamers Okeehumpkee and Astatula between Palatka and Silver Springs. Lanier names a “Colonel Hart, of Pilatka” as the holder of a canal charter.
plates.source: State Archives of Florida, Florida Memory, item 148613, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.

plates.caption: Freight rates to Jacksonville from Leesburg, by rail only, and from Sanford, on the river: “nearly twice the rate”; a box of oranges 10 cents by the old steamers, 26 cents by rail.
plates.source: House Document 514, 63rd Congress, 2nd Session (1914), p. 8; Internet Archive; public domain.

plates.caption: A river steamer on the Ocklawaha, Detroit Publishing Company photograph.
plates.source: Library of Congress, Detroit Publishing Company collection, LCCN 2008679617, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.

plates.caption: The Army's engineers recommend locks and a six-foot channel to Lake Dora, provided that local interests give the land free, hold the United States harmless for flooded land, and run a boat line free of the railroads.
plates.source: House Document 514, 63rd Congress, 2nd Session (1914), p. 2; Internet Archive; public domain.

plates.caption: The title of Florida's act of 12 May 1933 creating the Ship Canal Authority (none of the State's general revenues to be used; counties may condemn land and levy taxes), the directors, and the Legislature's memorial to the President.
plates.source: Documentary History of the Florida Canal, Senate Document 275, 74th Congress (1936), p. 82; University of Florida Digital Collections; public domain.

plates.caption: “Senator Turner on Ship Canal Authority”: the authority's organization meeting at Tallahassee, and an estimate of $114,000,000 to $160,000,000.
plates.source: Levy County Journal (Bronson), 8 June 1933, p. 1; Florida Digital Newspaper Library, University of Florida; no copyright renewal found.

plates.titel: Five million dollars for relief, 30 August 1935
plates.caption: The President's allotment from the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935: “To provide work relief and increase employment”, with the schedule of works.
plates.source: Documentary History of the Florida Canal, Senate Document 275, 74th Congress (1936), p. 155; University of Florida Digital Collections; public domain.

plates.caption: Representative Sears on the bond election of 22 October 1935: “At that election only freeholders could vote”, and the vote in each of the six counties.
plates.source: Documentary History of the Florida Canal, Senate Document 275, 74th Congress (1936), p. 382, detail; University of Florida Digital Collections; public domain.

plates.caption: The appraiser James A. Taylor before the House Committee on Rivers and Harbors: the price of the land, and “A great many of them are Negroes”.
plates.source: Hearings on H.R. 6150, House Committee on Rivers and Harbors (1937), p. 115; University of Florida Digital Collections; public domain.

plates.titel: Status of right of way acquisition, June 1936
plates.caption: The Army engineers' map of the western part of the route, from Ocala, Camp Roosevelt and Santos past Dunnellon to the Gulf near Inglis and Yankeetown, with the land under option, in condemnation and still required: 21,633 of 81,492 acres in possession.
plates.source: House Document 194, 75th Congress, 1st Session (1937), map sheet 1 (U.S. Engineer Office, Ocala, June 1936); U.S. Congressional Serial Set, scan of govinfo.gov; public domain.
